articles.title: The JWST May Have Found Where Heavy Black Hole Seeds Formed
articles.description: Astrophysicists think that black holes grow through a hierarchical merger framework. But the elusive Intermediate Mass Black Holes are the missing link between stellar mass black holes, and the gargantuan supermassive black holes like the one at the center of the Milky Way. The JWST may have found the ancient sources of IMBH heavy seeds: young massive clusters in the high-redshift Universe.
articles.summary: JWST observations may have uncovered evidence for intermediate-mass black hole seeds, potentially solving a major mystery about how supermassive black holes form in the early universe.

articles.title: NASA smashed into an asteroid. Now Hera is closing in to see what happened
articles.description: Europe’s Hera spacecraft has captured its first clear view of two asteroids involved in NASA’s historic 2022 experiment to redirect a potentially dangerous space rock. Now approaching the pair, Hera will investigate the mysterious aftermath of the collision and uncover why the asteroid shifted far more than scientists predicted.
articles.summary: Europe's Hera spacecraft has captured detailed images of the asteroids involved in NASA's groundbreaking 2022 kinetic impact experiment, providing crucial data on the mission's historic results.

articles.title: NASA’s Voyager 1 is about to reach a historic one-light-day milestone
articles.description: NASA’s Voyager 1 is approaching an extraordinary milestone nearly 50 years after its launch, even as engineers battle dwindling power and mysterious technical problems. A clever energy-saving maneuver has extended the spacecraft’s scientific mission, while an unexplained 48-hour communications blackout recently gave NASA a scare. On November 18, Voyager 1 will reach a distance of one light-day from Earth, making even the simplest round-trip communication take 48 hours.
articles.summary: Nearly 50 years after launch, NASA's Voyager 1 is approaching the remarkable milestone of traveling one light-day distance from Earth while continuing to transmit valuable scientific data.

articles.title: All 5 genetic “letters” of DNA and RNA discovered in a 4.5-billion-year-old asteroid
articles.description: Scientists have discovered all five essential nucleobases used in DNA and RNA in pristine samples from asteroid Ryugu, revealing that key ingredients for life existed in space billions of years ago. The remarkable finding adds to growing evidence from other asteroids and meteorites that these molecules were widespread throughout the early Solar System.
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered all five essential nucleobases of DNA and RNA in pristine samples from the asteroid Ryugu, providing compelling evidence of life's chemical building blocks in space.

articles.title: NASA's Hubble and Webb discover ancient worlds that remember their past
articles.description: NASA’s Hubble and James Webb Space Telescopes have uncovered surprising clues about the solar system’s origins by studying 27 tiny, distant objects beyond Neptune. Scientists discovered that these ancient building blocks of planets have remained remarkably unchanged for billions of years, while their unexpected sizes and numbers challenge existing theories of planet formation.
articles.summary: The Hubble and James Webb Space Telescopes have uncovered surprising insights into the solar system's ancient origins by studying distant planetary systems and their formation history.

articles.title: Scientists say a forgotten particle may explain why the universe exists
articles.description: A mysterious particle overlooked for decades may hold the key to why matter survived the Big Bang, allowing stars, planets, and life to exist. Scientists believe this forgotten neutrino reshaped the early universe and may have left detectable gravitational wave signals that could help unlock the cosmos’s deepest mysteries.
articles.summary: A long-overlooked particle may hold the key to explaining why matter persisted after the Big Bang, potentially solving one of physics' greatest mysteries about the universe's existence.

articles.title: Happy 65 Years: NASA’s Johnson Space Center Then and Now
articles.description: Sixty-five years ago, a bold vision took root in Houston: a NASA center dedicated to human spaceflight. Since its founding, NASA’s Johnson Space Center has helped lead the nation’s human spaceflight program, supporting missions from Project Mercury through Artemis. Today, Johnson serves as NASA’s Center of Excellence for Human Spaceflight, and its workforce is helping […]
articles.summary: NASA's Johnson Space Center celebrates 65 years of pioneering human spaceflight, reflecting on its historic contributions to space exploration.

articles.title: NASA’s Hubble Uncovers Case of Missing Oxygen in Nearby Dwarf Galaxies
articles.description: NASA’s Hubble studied 37 nearby dwarf galaxies and found that much of the oxygen they expected to see is missing.
articles.summary: NASA's Hubble Space Telescope reveals a mystery: dwarf galaxies contain less oxygen than expected, opening new questions about galactic evolution.

articles.title: Ghostly Cat’s Head Nebula lurks within sight of Hubble and Webb
articles.description: The NASA/ESA Hubble and the NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescopes recently stared at an eerie star-forming scene within the Carina Nebula, a massive gas and dust cloud located approximately 7500 light-years away from Earth. The two telescopes offer complementary views of the shadowy form, nicknamed the Cat’s Head Nebula, which reflects the 'magical'' process of star formation. Hubble’s visible-light view shows the cat as a dark, elongated dust pillar and hints of young forming stars, while Webb’s infrared-light imagery unveils many stars and other hidden details.
articles.summary: Hubble and James Webb telescopes capture stunning images of the Cat's Head Nebula, revealing the dynamic star-forming regions within this cosmic structure.

articles.title: MMX lifts off to Mars’s moon Phobos
articles.description:
Image:
			MMX lifts off to Mars’s moon Phobos
articles.summary: The MMX mission successfully launches toward Mars's moon Phobos, pioneering humanity's exploration of the Martian system's intriguing moons.

articles.title: Celebrating BepiColombo, three words at a time
articles.description:
Video: 
			00:03:32
				
BepiColombo launched on 20 October 2018. This year, the anniversary is special. After eight years of travelling through the inner Solar System, the ESA/JAXA mission will arrive at Mercury on 9 December, 2026. To celebrate, mission team members were asked to describe BepiColombo in just three words.
Their answers capture the character of the mission and the people behind it. Complex, collaborative and transformative are among the words chosen, reflecting both the demanding journey to Mercury and the international teamwork that has made it possible. Together, their words offer a personal snapshot of BepiColombo as it approaches its long-awaited destination.
articles.summary: BepiColombo celebrates eight years of journey toward Mercury, marking a landmark anniversary in this groundbreaking ESA-JAXA collaborative mission.

articles.title: Euclid discovers new comet
articles.description: The European Space Agency’s Euclid space telescope has discovered its first previously unknown comet, in images taken between 16 and 24 September 2026.
articles.summary: The Euclid space telescope discovers its first previously unknown comet, demonstrating the mission's exciting potential for new celestial discoveries.

articles.title: Mars moon lander set to launch on 19 October
articles.description:
The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission is set to launch into space on a H3 rocket from the Tanegashima Space Center at 04:41 JST on 20 October 2026 (20:41 BST / 21:41 CEST on 19 October 2026). MMX will be the first mission to collect a sample from Mars’s moon Phobos and bring it back to Earth. 
MMX is led by the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), in collaboration with the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), the French space agency (CNES), the German Aerospace Center (DLR) and the European Space Agency (ESA).
articles.summary: The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission is set to launch on October 19, beginning humanity's dedicated exploration of Mars's fascinating moons.

articles.title: Solar Orbiter tracks origin of mysterious magnetic switchbacks
articles.description: The European Space Agency-led Solar Orbiter spacecraft has flown through an S-shaped kink known as a ‘switchback’ in the solar wind’s magnetic field. By fingerprinting the elusive particles within the switchback, Solar Orbiter has traced its origin back to the Sun’s surface and revealed more about solar magnetism – the unruly instigator of dangerous solar storms.
articles.summary: ESA's Solar Orbiter has made breakthrough observations of magnetic switchbacks in the solar wind, mysterious S-shaped kinks that reveal new insights into solar magnetic behavior and particle acceleration.

articles.title: The Vera Rubin Has Found Two More of the Milky Way's Dim Satellites
articles.description: The Vera Rubin Observatory has detected two more of the Milky Ways' dim, hard to see satellites. One is an ultra-faint dwarf galaxy, and one is a globular cluster. Each one is a missing piece of the puzzle in the Milky Way's merger history. By finding more of these satellites, our understanding of galaxy growth, and the role dark matter plays in it, will improve.
articles.summary: The Vera Rubin Observatory has discovered two additional faint satellite galaxies orbiting the Milky Way, advancing our understanding of galactic structure and dark matter distribution.

articles.title: Space Outposts Beyond the Moon May Rely on Planetary AI
articles.description: NASA plans to return astronauts to the lunar surface in 2028 for the first time since Apollo 17 in 1972. But the famed agency has no intention of stopping there, as they plan to establish a permanent human presence on the Moon through a slow and meticulous process involving power, resource extraction, and habitat technologies. However, with the soaring use of artificial intelligence (AI) in our everyday lives, how could this emerging technology be used to identify new landing sites for future outposts on the Moon and possibly Mars?
articles.summary: NASA's lunar return plans for 2028 may leverage advanced AI systems at future space outposts, envisioning intelligent autonomous support for human exploration beyond the Moon.

articles.title: Hera Probe Sees Asteroid Pair Separately for First Time
articles.description: Planetary defense is a growing concern among the scientific community, as efforts have been made to design and implement missions meant to deflect incoming threats to the Earth well in advance. In 2022, NASA intentionally collided the Double Asteroid Redirection test (DART) planetary defense spacecraft into the smaller asteroid of the binary asteroid, Didymos and Dimorphos, with the latter being the smaller one. While the goal was to ascertain if deflecting an asteroid is feasible, how did this influence the geological characteristics of Dimorphos, and what can it teach us about planetary defense missions?
articles.summary: The Hera probe has achieved the first separate observations of a binary asteroid system, advancing planetary defense capabilities and asteroid characterization technology.

articles.title: A tiny shift exposes a cold brown dwarf masquerading as an early galaxy
articles.description: A faint red object spotted by the James Webb Space Telescope originally appeared to offer a possible glimpse of the universe's first galaxies. But images taken about 3½ years apart revealed a giveaway: The object, nicknamed Capotauro, had moved.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: JWST observations revealed a faint red object as a cold brown dwarf rather than an early galaxy, demonstrating the telescope's precision in distinguishing nearby and distant objects.

articles.title: Leviathan's sprawling stars challenge idea that dusty giants become compact galaxies
articles.description: Astronomers using the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) have confirmed a massive, dust-rich galaxy called Leviathan in the early universe. Seen when the universe was roughly 1.5 billion years old, the galaxy has its stars spread out rather than in a concentrated fashion. A paper, describing its strange stellar distribution, was posted to the arXiv preprint server on Oct. 19.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: JWST has confirmed the existence of Leviathan, a massive dust-rich galaxy in the early universe, challenging current models of how galaxies evolve and compact over time.

articles.title: Queen's University Belfast students find Neptune's elusive Trojan asteroids
articles.description: An international team led by researchers at Queen's University Belfast has made a discovery that has eluded astronomers for decades. Beginning in 1906, telescope observations revealed a population of asteroids leading and trailing Jupiter, which came to be known as the "Trojan" and "Greek" populations. Since then, astronomers have discovered similar "families" orbiting Saturn and Uranus, but not Neptune. Thanks to the Queen's-led team, the mystery of the missing Trojans has now been resolved.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Researchers have discovered elusive Trojan asteroids orbiting Neptune, a long-sought discovery that expands our understanding of the outer solar system's small body populations.

articles.title: Scientists build whole-Earth simulation to help find life on other planets
articles.description: It's a dizzyingly busy time for scientists searching for life on distant planets. To date, astronomers have cataloged more than 6,000 planets beyond our solar system and are searching the atmospheres of the most promising worlds for chemicals that might be byproducts of life. Astrobiologists are particularly interested in atmospheres like Earth's that trap enough heat to support liquid water on the planet's surface, which scientists consider the key factor in determining whether a planet can support life as we know it.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Scientists have created a whole-Earth simulation model to improve detection of biosignatures on exoplanets, advancing the search for life beyond our solar system.

articles.title: NASA’s Perseverance Mars rover breaks historic record after traveling 28 miles
articles.description: NASA’s Perseverance rover has set a historic record by traveling 28.10 miles across Mars, farther than any vehicle has ever driven on another world. Armed with groundbreaking autonomous navigation technology and increasingly advanced driving capabilities, the rover is pushing the boundaries of robotic exploration.
articles.summary: NASA's Perseverance rover has set a historic distance record by traveling 28.10 miles across Mars, surpassing all previous rover achievements on the Red Planet.

articles.title: IceCube detects ghost particles with 10 billion times the energy of solar neutrinos
articles.description: Mysterious particles called neutrinos constantly stream through our bodies, and scientists are now detecting incredibly powerful versions arriving from distant cosmic sources using a massive observatory buried in Antarctic ice. These elusive “ghost particles” could hold extraordinary clues about the Big Bang, extreme cosmic events, and some of the universe’s greatest mysteries.
articles.summary: The IceCube detector has captured ultra-high-energy neutrinos with 10 billion times more energy than solar neutrinos, opening new windows into the cosmos's most energetic phenomena.

articles.title: Scientists just found a loophole that could let black holes split in two
articles.description: Scientists have discovered a possible loophole in the laws that normally prevent black holes from splitting apart, suggesting that extremely fast-spinning black holes might divide into two. The surprising finding raises the possibility of an entirely new black hole phenomenon that future telescopes could potentially detect.
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered a theoretical loophole suggesting that under certain conditions, black holes might be able to split apart, challenging conventional understanding of black hole physics.

articles.title: Why does Betelgeuse keep fading? The mystery of Orion's giant star
articles.description: From stellar pulsations to giant dust clouds and a mysterious companion, astronomers are piecing together why Betelguese keeps changing brightness.
articles.summary: Astronomers are unraveling the mystery behind Betelgeuse's periodic fading, uncovering clues from stellar pulsations, dust clouds, and a potential companion star.

articles.title: James Webb Space Telescope uncovers new clues about the origins of 'interstellar invader' comet 3I/ATLAS
articles.description: The findings are another clue towards understanding the origins of 3I/ATLAS and the planet-forming conditions around other stars.
articles.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope has revealed new insights into the origins of interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS and the planetary formation conditions around other stars.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 2, 2000: Expedition 1 Arrives at the International Space Station
articles.description: Expedition 1 crewmates Bill Shepherd, Yuri Gidzenko and Sergei Krikalev pose with a model of the space station as it appeared in 2000.
articles.summary: Expedition 1 crew members arrived at the International Space Station on November 2, 2000, marking the historic beginning of continuous human presence in low Earth orbit.

articles.title: Nanohertz Gravitational-Wave Constraints on Supermassive Binary Black Holes at Cosmic Dawn
articles.description: Author(s): Yiqin Chen, Shi-Yi Zhao, Xingjiang Zhu, N. D. Ramesh Bhat, Jacob Cardinal Tremblay, Małgorzata Curyło, Valentina Di Marco, George Hobbs, Wenhua Ling, Rami F. Mandow, Richard N. Manchester, Saurav Mishra, Daniel J. Reardon, Sparrow Roch, Christopher…
articles.summary: Nanohertz gravitational waves provide new constraints on supermassive binary black holes in the early universe, advancing our understanding of cosmic evolution at cosmic dawn.

articles.title: Two Different Kinds of Gamma-Ray Bursts Erupted 4 Minutes Apart. Astronomers Have Never Seen This Before.
articles.description: Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) are among the most energetic cosmic events since the Big Bang, releasing the most energetic type of radiation, gamma rays – the stuff that turned unassuming Bruce Banner into the rampaging Hulk, but on an astronomical, potentially plan…
articles.summary: For the first time, astronomers observed two distinct gamma-ray bursts erupting just 4 minutes apart, revealing new insights into these most energetic cosmic phenomena.

articles.title: Figuring out where cosmic neutrinos come from is tricky - radio telescopes could help find where these ‘ghost particles’ originate
articles.description: A researcher just won a Nobel Prize for detecting tiny particles from space. Scientists now want to get better at figuring out where in the cosmos they come from.
articles.summary: Radio telescopes are emerging as powerful tools to pinpoint the cosmic origins of ghostly neutrinos, following a Nobel Prize-winning detection breakthrough.
